mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods when UNRATE exceeds 5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings for industrial firms and drags the S&P 500 lower over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO falls for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in FEDFUNDS and a decline in CPIAUCSL (core inflation) over two months signals a 'disinflationary tightening' regime, where higher rates and lower inflation jointly compress risk premia and depress equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises AND CPIAUCSL falls over two months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of simultaneous FEDFUNDS increases and CPIAUCSL declines over two months.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive momentum in real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) combined with a rising housing starts index (HOUST) signals robust household demand, which boosts corporate revenues and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and HOUST both rise for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both PAYEMS and HOUST rise for two consecutive months in an early-cycle regime.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above 0.5% month-over-month for two consecutive months signals a strong labor market, which supports consumer spending and corporate profitability, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > +0.5% MoM for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS rises by more than 0.5% month-over-month for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) for three consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces revenue growth for consumer-facing companies and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, except during periods of strong monetary easing.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS declines for three consecutive months AND FEDFUNDS is not falling
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS declines for three months and FEDFUNDS is stable or rising.
